chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who doubts after he has performed sajdah that he did not perform ruku‘.

He said: “He should continue in his salat (prayer) until he becomes certain that he did not perform ruku‘. If he becomes certain that he did not perform ruku‘, then let him cast aside the two sajdahs for which there was no ruku‘ and build upon his salat (prayer) which is upon completion. But if he does not become certain until after he has finished and departed, then let him stand and perform one rak‘ah and two sajdahs, and there is nothing upon him.”
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts after sajdah that he missed the ruku‘ in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about doubt regarding a missed ruku‘ in salat (prayer) after performing sajdah. It distinguishes between doubt during the prayer and certainty after completion, outlining how the worshipper should continue or make up what was missed. It is significant in the fiqh of sahw because it clarifies how prayer is corrected when uncertainty turns into certainty.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1006 - Al-‘Ala' narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:

"If a man doubts after prostrating that he has not bowed (rak'a), he should continue with his prayer until he is certain that he did not bow. If he becomes certain that he did not bow, then he should perform the two prostrations (sajdatayn) that have no bowing and complete his prayer as though it were perfect.
However, if he does not become certain until after he has finished and turned away from the prayer, he should stand up and pray one more rak'ah with two prostrations, and there is no harm upon him."
